Verification and limits

Lint, typecheck, and the fast aggregate passed. Lint reported five warnings and one informational diagnostic. Turbo reused 11 of 12 typecheck tasks and 6 of 7 test tasks. The aggregate reports 2,477 passing tests, 181 skipped tests, and zero failures.

Additional focused scans ran 23 worker and 42 domain tests. The publication finding was reproduced with an injected store failure. The PostgreSQL suites, production build, production dependency audit, hosted deployment, long-running race, and real social delivery were not executed in this review.

The app has established ownership modules, database gates, structured failures, and a consistent visual foundation. Findings target gaps in those existing mechanisms. No code edits, migrations, deployments, or social posts were made. The requested test import created one Project and started its processing.

Keep the monorepo and existing database/process adapters. No evidence here warrants microservices, sharding, a generic event bus, or compatibility paths. Fix the two P1s and complete the existing gates before launch; then tighten progress, worker operation, and browsing limits.

Live import result: Passed: import, normalization, transcription, and detection completed. The Project contains 10 clips. Auto-render was off, so render/export and publication were not tested. Open the test Project.

Recover Campaign Operation outcomes after a committed Social Post

Reproduced through the real scheduling module with an injected settlement failure.

Before

After

flowchart TD

after1["Retain the same intent identity"]

Problem
A Social Post commits, then item settlement fails. The catch records ineligible with no Social Post ID. A corrected submission can create a second post.
Change
Concentrate admission-outcome recovery in the Campaign Operation module. Recover the existing deterministic publication identity before reporting a committed result as failed.
Benefits
Depth hides the two-commit protocol; locality keeps uncertainty handling at one seam; leverage protects every campaign caller.
Deletion test
Deleting the broad catch removes false certainty. The remaining recovery belongs inside this module, rather than in browser callers.
Verification
Inject failure after admission, during result read, and during item settlement. Replay through the scheduling interface must recover the original Social Post, including with the PostgreSQL adapter.
Aligns with ADR 0007. Successful items must not be repeated in a corrected selection.

Give Ingest Jobs ownership-checked settlement and a durable handoff

Source-confirmed race; not induced against the running app.

Before

flowchart TD
before0["Download allowed 45–60 min"]
before1["Reaper expires at 30 min"]
before2["Replacement worker starts"]
before3["Old worker can overwrite"]
before0 --> before1
before1 --> before2
before2 --> before3
classDef focus fill:#fff0ed,stroke:#bb4935,color:#762a20;
class before0,before1,before2,before3 focus;

After

flowchart TD
after0["Ingest Job module"]
after1["Renew and verify ownership"]
after2["Atomic source + job outcome"]
after3["Durable generation intent"]
after0 --> after1
after1 --> after2
after2 --> after3
classDef focus fill:#173c36,stroke:#173c36,color:#ffffff;
class after0,after1,after2,after3 focus;
Problem
The reaper requeues jobs after 30 minutes, but downloads may run for 45–60 minutes. Old workers settle by job ID without claim ownership, and the reaper updates the Project separately.
Change
Deepen the separate Ingest Job module so claim ownership, renewal, settlement, reaping, and durable generation handoff share one policy.
Benefits
Depth removes ordering rules from worker callers; locality joins ownership and handoff; leverage covers link and file ingest at their shared seam.
Deletion test
Move the scattered lifecycle writes into one module. Its removal would scatter real ownership rules, so the module earns its keep.
Verification
Race a slow live import, stale completion, stale failure, and reaper settlement through the lifecycle interface and database adapter. Crash after source acceptance; generation must recover automatically.
Preserve ADR 0001: Ingest Jobs stay distinct from Workflow Runs. This does not require a generic queue or compatibility path.

03
P2Strongprocess adapter

Keep YouTube dependency failure within link intake

Source-confirmed startup and exit coupling.

Before

YouTube token process
↓
Whole worker availability
↓
Billing, publishing, rendering stop

After

Worker remains available
↓
Link intake readiness seam
↓
YouTube failure stays local
Problem
All loops wait for the YouTube token process, and its later exit shuts down the whole worker. One import dependency can stop billing reconciliation, publishing, and other processing.
Change
Contain YouTube readiness and failure in the link intake module. Reuse the Worker Process Module for subprocess lifetime policy.
Benefits
Locality limits the outage; leverage reuses the process adapter; depth keeps dependency recovery behind the intake seam.
Deletion test
Remove the duplicated TERM-to-KILL implementation. Lifecycle complexity concentrates in the existing deep process module.
Verification
Fail token startup, occupy its port, terminate it after startup, and cancel import work. Verify unrelated loops continue and process cleanup follows the existing interface.
The current direct spawn/kill implementation diverges from ADR 0011. This recommendation restores that decision.

04
P2Strongin-process + process adapter

Make worker shutdown reach active Workflow Attempts

Source-confirmed signal gap; no live SIGTERM injected.

Before

SIGTERM
↓
Polling stops
↓
Active attempt keeps heartbeat
↓
Host eventually kills process

After

Worker lifetime module
↓
Stop claims
↓
Bounded drain or cancellation
↓
Reap processes; recover work
Problem
SIGTERM stops polling and aborts workerShutdown, but active Workflow Attempts use another controller and keep renewing leases. Deployment can end in a hosting force-kill.
Change
Give the worker execution module one bounded shutdown policy that reaches active work while preserving Workflow Attempt fencing.
Benefits
Depth hides shutdown ordering; locality puts cancellation at one seam; leverage uses the process adapter already capable of cancellation.
Deletion test
Replace the partial shutdown handler with complete lifetime ownership. Adding a second independent shutdown module would only move the problem.
Verification
Send SIGTERM during an active render. Verify no new claims, bounded exit, descendant reaping, and recoverable work through the execution interface.
Aligns with ADRs 0001 and 0011. Preserve ownership-loss semantics.

05
P2Strongin-process + database/browser adapters

Use one Project progress meaning across filtering and refresh

Confirmed in Chrome: the test Project appeared under Ready while Detect was running.

Before

Ingest → filter
↓
Ingest + transcript → badge
↓
Ingest + transcript → refresh
↓
Workflow Runs → detail

After

Intake + Workflow Runs
↓
Project progress module
↓
Consistent filter and badge
↓
Refresh until useful outcome
Problem
The filter reads ingest state, while badges and refresh also read transcription. Detection and rendering are absent, so Ready can mean clips are still being created and refresh can stop too early.
Change
Concentrate the product meaning of Project progress in one module, used by list membership, badges, counts, and refresh eligibility.
Benefits
Depth hides lifecycle interpretation; locality fixes status once; leverage gives every browser adapter the same meaning across the seam.
Deletion test
Delete the divergent shallow interpretations after consolidation. Retaining them beside a new formatter would preserve the inconsistency.
Verification
Cover queued, running, failed, and completed stages through the progress interface and query adapter. Follow transcription into detection without manually refreshing the list.
No ADR conflict. Underlying intake and Workflow Run lifecycles remain distinct.

P2Worth exploringdatabase + browser adapters

Bound library work while keeping every result reachable

Source-confirmed limits and full-history polling; no load benchmark performed.

Before

Exports → first 200 only
↓
Picker → first 500 only
↓
Posts → all history repeatedly

After

Bounded list module
↓
Reachable continuation
↓
Searchable clip selection
↓
Bounded live-state refresh
Problem
Exports stop at 200 and the Calendar picker at 500 without continuation. Project Social Posts have no equivalent bound and the browser rereads all history every 5 or 30 seconds.
Change
Let each domain list module own bounded navigation and continuation. Add a searchable Calendar picker and refresh active publication outcomes separately from history.
Benefits
Depth makes completeness and cost part of the interface; locality keeps paging at the query seam; leverage simplifies each browser adapter.
Deletion test
Deleting caps alone moves cost into database and browser memory. Add continuation to the existing modules, without a general query framework.
Verification
Create more than 200 exports and 500 clips in disposable fixtures; reach the final item. Check traversal during inserts and bound recurring publication payloads.
No ADR conflict. Prioritize before a larger beta, after correctness fixes.

P2Stronglocal-substitutable PostgreSQL adapter

Close the gap between documented and enforced database gates

CI and repository verification tests enumerate six domains; package scripts define eight.

Before

Eight documented DB gates
↓
Six CI entries
↓
Test asserts those same six

After

Complete gate inventory
↓
Eight isolated CI executions
↓
Omissions fail verification
Problem
CI omits test:brand-profiles:db and test:vizard-expansion:db. These exercise tenant isolation, asset deletion races, campaign claim loss, review access, and other durable behavior.
Change
Run the two existing gates in CI and update the verification inventory so newly documented gates cannot silently be omitted.
Benefits
Leverage comes from existing deep tests; locality keeps gate coverage explicit; the PostgreSQL adapter verifies behavior mocks cannot establish.
Deletion test
This is a verification gap, not a reason for a new module. Remove the stale six-domain assumption rather than building test orchestration machinery.
Verification
Run both omitted commands with disposable schemas, and verify CI executes them. Keep domain assertions at the real module interface and database seam.
No ADR conflict. Useful immediate work alongside the P1 fixes.

08
P2Strongbrowser adapter

Make publishing readiness readable on a phone

Observed at 390 × 844 in Chrome. Footer labels crowd together; see screenshot 05.

Before

One row at every width
↓
Timing | timezone | count | submit
↓
Readiness reason above the fold

After

Publishing module, narrow layout
↓
Timing + timezone row
↓
Readiness reason + count
↓
Clear submission action
Problem
The fixed footer keeps timing buttons, a nonwrapping timezone, post count, and submission in one row. At phone width the timezone and count overlap; the disabled action gives no nearby reason.
Change
Make the existing publishing module layout stack at narrow widths and show its current blocking reason beside the final action. Put editable copy ahead of secondary regeneration controls.
Benefits
Locality keeps readiness with submission; leverage reuses the existing validation implementation; depth improves the user interface without adding a new seam or adapter.
Deletion test
Keep the existing publishing module. Delete the forced single-row layout; extracting another shallow visual module would not fix the constraint.
Verification
Check 320px and 390px, a long timezone, multiple accounts, and the previous-submission label. Verify keyboard focus and visible disabled-action guidance.
No ADR conflict. Screenshot evidence supports layout findings, not a full accessibility certification.

Observed product flow

Screenshots captured in this run. Development timing is not a production benchmark. Review covers the shown paths, not every role, empty state, keyboard path, or accessibility requirement.

Top recommendation

Recover Campaign Operation outcomes first.

A false failure can cause an unintended duplicate publication for the first real user. Start with candidate 01, then close Ingest Job ownership and handoff gaps. Both improve existing modules without widening the product.

Prepared as a review, not an implementation plan. Concrete interface design follows candidate selection. Screenshots are embedded; Tailwind and Mermaid load from CDN. The custom CSS remains readable without them. Static structure and embedded images were checked; automated browser rendering verification was blocked by the local-file URL policy.
